result.title: Scaling Laws for Generative Reward Models
result.summary: We study generative reward models (GenRMs) as online preference providers for policy optimization in creative writing. Across Qwen3 reward-model sizes from 0.6B to 14B, Thinking judges trained with GRPO have higher static Gold-label accuracy than Answer-Only judges trained with SFT. This ranking often reverses when the judges train policies through online DPO: Answer-Only rewarders yield higher peak and top-five-average policy Elo in seven of eight matched settings under a fixed, learned 32B Gold evaluator. Intermediate Thinking-judge checkpoints can also outperform later, more statically accurate checkpoints as rewarders. Sweeps over rewarder size, policy size, training duration and DPO regularization show substantial benefits from reward-model capacity, including judges larger than the policy. We analyze trajectories with evaluator-specific Elo arenas, conditional match-resampling intervals and descriptive scaling fits. These results demonstrate an evaluator-rewarder gap in the studied pipelines: fixed-distribution judging accuracy does not determine downstream optimization quality. The comparison changes judge-training objective as well as response format, and the main ranking is conditional on its learned reference rather than a universal human-quality result. A limited follow-up using a different learned judge is inconclusive overall.

AI.brief_summary: 在创意写作的在线 DPO 流程中比较 0.6B–14B 的生成式奖励模型：GRPO 训练的 Thinking 评判者静态金标准确率更高，但作为在线奖励提供者时常不如 SFT 的 Answer-Only 评判者，且中间检查点可能优于更晚的检查点。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「评判准确率不能决定下游优化质量」及中间检查点更优的现象，可能为 LVR 中推理轨迹训练与贡献分配提供可核查线索，即静态指标与 latent 状态实际被使用程度之间的错位。
